key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage that preferentially occurs at the hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide buried-interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification improving UV stability in perovskite films and devices.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements during UV light-soaking.
Compare films and devices with different indium tin oxide interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Non-destructive measurements localized preferential UV degradation to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and indicated reduced damage after interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or evidence that UV-test improvements translate to long-term performance under full-spectrum operation.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
